grammar.countability: uncountable for polite behavior; countable for a polite act or privilege

usage.uncountable: Courtesy without an article commonly means polite and considerate behavior.
usage.countable: A courtesy is a particular considerate act, privilege, or conventional gesture.
usage.attributive: Before a noun, courtesy can indicate something provided free of charge or performed as a polite gesture.
usage.courtesy_of: Courtesy of identifies the person or organization providing something and can also indicate the source of an image or material.
usage.sarcasm: Courtesy of may be used ironically to identify the unwelcome cause of a problem.

ja: 他人への敬意・配慮を示す礼儀正しい態度
相手への思いやりから行う個別の親切・便宜
社会・職業上、礼儀として期待される行為
形容詞的に、無料で提供されるサービス・設備

en: polite and considerate behavior showing respect for other people
an individual act of kindness, consideration, or accommodation
an action conventionally expected as a matter of social or professional politeness
attributively, a service or facility provided without charge
in courtesy of, through the kindness, provision, or sponsorship of a person or organization
a formula identifying the source that supplied an image, item, or information

nuance.ja: courtesy は、単なる作法の知識ではなく、相手を尊重し負担を減らそうとする態度や行為を表す。He had the courtesy to call. は「彼には電話をする程度の礼儀はあった」という意味で、文脈によっては非難を含む。as a courtesy は、法的義務ではなく配慮として行うことを示す場合があるが、この表現だけで法的義務の有無が決まるわけではない。courtesy copy は正式な送達・提出とは別に参考として送る写し、courtesy bus は顧客向けの無料送迎車である。courtesy of the storm のような皮肉な用法では、「嵐のおかげで」という好ましくない原因を示す。
nuance.en: Courtesy concerns not merely knowledge of etiquette but conduct intended to respect others and reduce inconvenience. He had the courtesy to call means that he showed at least the expected consideration by calling and may carry an implied criticism. As a courtesy can indicate that an act is voluntary rather than legally required, but the phrase itself does not determine whether a legal obligation exists. A courtesy copy is supplied for information separately from formal service or filing, while a courtesy bus is free transportation for customers. In an ironic expression such as courtesy of the storm, courtesy of identifies an unwelcome cause.

ja: courtesy：相手への敬意・配慮を示す礼儀正しさ、または個別の親切。
politeness：失礼にならない言葉遣い・態度を広く表す。
civility：対立があっても保たれる、最低限の礼節ある振る舞い。
etiquette：特定の社会・職業・場面で守るべき作法・慣例。
manners：人が社会生活で示す行儀・振る舞い。
kindness：人を助けたい、苦痛を減らしたいという親切心と行為。
favor：人のために行う個別の親切・便宜。
complimentary：商品・サービスが無料で提供されることを明確に表す。
en: courtesy is respectful consideration for others or a particular considerate act.
politeness broadly describes language and behavior that avoid giving offense.
civility is a basic level of respectful conduct maintained even during disagreement.
etiquette is the accepted code of behavior for a particular society, profession, or occasion.
manners are a person’s socially observable standards of behavior.
kindness is the desire and action to help people or reduce their distress.
a favor is an individual helpful act performed for another person.
complimentary explicitly means that a product or service is supplied free of charge.

etymology.ja: 古フランス語 curteisie「宮廷風の礼儀、上品な振る舞い」に由来し、court「宮廷」と同じ語族に属する。もとは宮廷にふさわしい洗練された態度や騎士的な作法を表した。そこから身分や場所を問わず、他人への礼儀・配慮・親切を広く意味するようになった。courteous「礼儀正しい」も同じ起源を持つ。courtesy service のような無料提供の意味は、顧客への厚意としてサービスを行うという発想から生じた。
etymology.en: Courtesy comes from Old French curteisie, meaning courtly manners or refined conduct, and belongs to the same word family as court. It originally described behavior considered appropriate at a royal or noble court, including refinement and chivalrous manners. Its meaning broadened to respectful and considerate conduct toward others regardless of rank or setting. Courteous shares the same origin. The free-of-charge sense in expressions such as courtesy service developed from the idea of providing something as a considerate gesture to a customer or guest.

note.ja: 言葉遣い・態度が社会的に適切で、相手に不快感を与えないこと。
note.en: Socially appropriate language or behavior that avoids offending others.

note.ja: 意見の対立がある状況でも相手に示す、節度ある礼儀正しさ。
note.en: Restrained and respectful conduct, particularly when people disagree.

note.ja: 自分の行動が相手の感情・事情・必要性に及ぼす影響への配慮。
note.en: Attention to how one’s conduct affects another person’s feelings, circumstances, or needs.

note.ja: 相手を助けたり苦痛を減らしたりしようとする思いやり。
note.en: Concern expressed through an effort to help another person or reduce their distress.

note.ja: 相手を助けるために行う具体的な親切・便宜。
note.en: A specific helpful act performed for another person.

ja: He had the courtesy to inform us that he would be late. — 彼には、遅れることを私たちに知らせるだけの礼儀はあった。
Please treat every visitor with courtesy and respect. — すべての来訪者に礼儀と敬意をもって接してください。
The hotel provides a courtesy bus to the airport. — そのホテルは空港まで無料送迎バスを運行している。
As a professional courtesy, we sent opposing counsel a copy of the document. — 職業上の礼儀として、私たちは相手方代理人にその書類の写しを送った。
The patent attorney provided a courtesy copy of the response, but warned that it did not constitute formal service. — 弁理士は応答書の参考用写しを提供したが、それは正式な送達には当たらないと注意を促した。
en: He had the courtesy to inform us that he would be late.
Please treat every visitor with courtesy and respect.
The hotel provides a courtesy bus to the airport.
As a professional courtesy, we sent opposing counsel a copy of the document.
The patent attorney provided a courtesy copy of the response, but warned that it did not constitute formal service.

patterns: be courteous in dealing with + person
it was courteous of someone to do

usage.person: Courteous commonly describes a person who behaves with politeness and respect.
usage.behavior: It can also modify conduct or communication: a courteous reply.
usage.preposition: Use to or toward / towards for the person receiving the courtesy.
usage.evaluation: Use of plus a person after an impersonal construction: It was courteous of her to reply.
usage.comparison: More courteous and most courteous are preferred to courteser and courtest.
usage.spelling: The standard spelling is courteous, not courtus; the middle vowel sequence reflects its relationship with courtesy.

ja: 他人に礼儀正しく敬意を示す
相手の感情や事情に配慮した、丁重な
発言・返答・態度などが失礼でなく、節度のある
対立や不満があっても礼節を保っている
en: polite and respectful toward other people
considerate of another person’s feelings or circumstances
for a reply, manner, or action, properly respectful and not offensive
maintaining civility despite disagreement or dissatisfaction

nuance.ja: courteous は、表面的に丁寧な言葉を使うだけでなく、相手を尊重し、その立場や負担に配慮して振る舞うことを表す。polite とほぼ同義だが、courteous の方がやや形式的で、職業上の応対・書面・公的な場面に適している。courteous but firm は、相手への敬意を保ちながらも、要求・期限・反対意見を曖昧にしない姿勢を表す。相手の意見に同意することまでは意味せず、厳しい拒絶や反論も courteous に伝えることができる。
nuance.en: Courteous describes more than the use of polite words; it suggests behavior that respects another person and takes account of their position or convenience. It is close to polite but somewhat more formal and especially natural for professional service, correspondence, and public conduct. Courteous but firm describes maintaining respect while clearly communicating a demand, deadline, or disagreement. Courtesy does not require agreement, so even a strong refusal or objection can be expressed courteously.

ja: courteous：相手への敬意と配慮を示す、やや形式的な「礼儀正しい」。
polite：社会的な作法に従い、失礼でないことを表す最も一般的な語。
civil：対立・不満があっても、最低限の礼節を保っている。
considerate：自分の行動が相手の感情・必要性に及ぼす影響をよく考える。
respectful：相手の地位・権利・感情などに敬意を示す。
gracious：親切で品があり、相手を快適にさせる寛大な態度を示す。
deferential：目上の人や権威ある人に敬意を示して控えめに振る舞う。
courtly：宮廷風に洗練され、儀礼的に丁重な。古風・文学的。
en: courteous means showing respectful consideration and is somewhat more formal than polite.
polite is the most general word for behaving according to accepted manners and avoiding offense.
civil means maintaining a basic level of politeness despite disagreement or hostility.
considerate means thinking carefully about how one’s conduct affects another person’s feelings or needs.
respectful means showing regard for another person’s status, rights, feelings, or dignity.
gracious suggests kind, dignified, and generous behavior that makes others feel comfortable.
deferential means respectfully yielding or showing restraint toward a senior or authoritative person.
courtly means refined and ceremoniously polite in an old-fashioned or literary manner.

etymology.ja: 古フランス語 corteis「宮廷風の、礼儀正しい」に由来し、court「宮廷」と同じ語族に属する。もとは宮廷にふさわしい洗練された作法や騎士的な態度を表した。そこから、身分や場所を問わず、人に敬意と配慮を示す「礼儀正しい」という一般的な意味へ広がった。名詞 courtesy も同じ起源を持つ。綴りは courtus ではなく courteous であり、語末の -eous はおおむね /iəs/ と発音される。
etymology.en: Courteous comes from Old French corteis, meaning courtly or polite, and belongs to the same word family as court. It originally described refined manners and chivalrous conduct considered appropriate at a royal or noble court. Its meaning broadened to respectful and considerate behavior toward others in any social setting. The noun courtesy shares the same origin. The standard spelling is courteous rather than courtus, and the final sequence is pronounced approximately /iəs/.

note.ja: 一般に認められた作法に従い、相手に失礼のないよう振る舞う。
note.en: Behaving according to accepted manners and avoiding offense.

note.ja: 親しみや好意がなくても、対立相手に最低限の礼儀を示す。
note.en: Maintaining a minimum level of politeness even without friendliness or agreement.

note.ja: 相手の感情・負担・都合を考えて行動する。
note.en: Taking account of another person’s feelings, burden, or convenience.

note.ja: 人の尊厳・地位・意見などを尊重する態度を示す。
note.en: Showing regard for another person’s dignity, position, or views.

note.ja: 礼儀正しさに加え、温かさ・品格・寛大さを感じさせる。
note.en: Showing warmth, dignity, and generosity in addition to politeness.

ja: The receptionist was courteous and helpful throughout our visit. — 受付係は、私たちの滞在中ずっと礼儀正しく親切だった。
It was courteous of her to inform us about the delay in advance. — 遅延について事前に知らせてくれたのは、彼女の丁重な配慮だった。
Even when the discussion became heated, he remained courteous. — 議論が白熱しても、彼は礼儀正しい態度を崩さなかった。
Our reply should be courteous but firm about the payment deadline. — 私たちの返答は丁重でありながら、支払期限については毅然としたものであるべきだ。
The patent attorney sent a courteous response explaining why the proposed amendment could not be accepted. — 弁理士は、提案された補正を受け入れられない理由を説明する丁重な返答を送った。
en: The receptionist was courteous and helpful throughout our visit.
It was courteous of her to inform us about the delay in advance.
Even when the discussion became heated, he remained courteous.
Our reply should be courteous but firm about the payment deadline.
The patent attorney sent a courteous response explaining why the proposed amendment could not be accepted.
